abstract: Multilingualism is the ability to converse fluently in more than one language. In multilingual societies, code-switching, the practise of switching languages during a conversation, occurs often, creating a need for multilingual dialogue and voice recognition systems in natural language processing (NLP). However, interpreting code-switching utterances is extremely difficult for these NLP systems, as the model must adjust to code-switching patterns. In recent years, deep learning strategies have enabled natural language systems with massive volumes of training data to attain human-level performance in languages. However, they cannot accommodate a large number of low-resource languages, mostly mixed languages. Also, code-switching, despite being a common occurrence, is unique to spoken language and lacks the transcriptions necessary for training deep learning models. Our work in this paper, explores the usage of multi-task learning in code-switched setting to see if it can leverage from the training signals of related tasks and improve the generalizability as well as boost the performance and metrics of our model.

bibliographic.title: Leveraging Multi-Task Learning in Code-Switched setting

content.problem: NLP systems struggle to interpret code-switched language because models must adapt to language-mixing patterns, and code-switched data is scarce and lacks the transcriptions needed to train deep learning models.
content.proposed_solution: The authors propose a multi-task learning framework with hard parameter sharing that couples a pre-trained multilingual transformer encoder with a bidirectional LSTM and shared MLP layers, plus task-specific MLP-CRF heads and an uncertainty-weighted joint loss, so that a primary token classification task can benefit from the training signals of a related task.
content.algorithm_or_model: Multi-task hard-parameter-sharing architecture of transformer encoder, BiLSTM and shared MLPs with task-specific MLP-CRF layers
dataset_testbed: LinCE benchmark (Named Entity Recognition and Language Identification tasks, Hindi-English)

content.claim: Multi-task learning in a code-switched setting outperforms the traditional single-task approach, with the NER task leveraging signals from the related language identification task to improve generalizability and F1 performance across all tested pre-trained models.
author_stated_limitations: The authors have not yet evaluated their framework on the GLUECoS benchmark or explored further optimizations, so results beyond LinCE remain untested.

evidence.problem_quote: However, they cannot accommodate a large number of low-resource languages, mostly mixed languages. Also, code-switching, despite being a common occurrence, is unique to spoken language and lacks the transcriptions necessary for training deep learning models.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: We have developed a framework that employs multi-task learning using a encoder, bidirectional LSTM [13] and multi-layer perceptron model as our primary architecture for token classification tasks.
evidence.claim_quote: The experimental results demonstrates that the multitask learning approach outperforms the traditional single-task approach (i.e using a model to train a single task) to solving the task by having an implicit data augmentation effect to help generalizability.
author_stated_limitation_quotes: We are yet to experiment on GLUECoS dataset and try out more optimizations in order to achieve much better results than the existing ones.
